check.name: lens.tests
check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

message.text: The rewritten test builds Melian's fake install under `mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "melian-install-"))` and never realpaths it. The faked `fileURLToPath` then returns `join(melian, "src", "mutation-enumeration.ts")` under the unresolved path. `TypeScriptMutationAdapter.open` realpaths the resolved instrumenter (`module`) and then compares it with `ancestorInstalls(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` through `path.relative`. When `tmpdir()` is a symlink, as macOS's `/var/folders/...` is (it resolves to `/private/var/...`), `module` is never inside any of those ancestors. The `source === "melian"` guard on line 143 then rejects the entry whatever line 140 does.

explanation.what: The rewritten test builds Melian's fake install under `mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "melian-install-"))` and never realpaths it. The faked `fileURLToPath` then returns `join(melian, "src", "mutation-enumeration.ts")` under the unresolved path. `TypeScriptMutationAdapter.open` realpaths the resolved instrumenter (`module`) and then compares it with `ancestorInstalls(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` through `path.relative`. When `tmpdir()` is a symlink, as macOS's `/var/folders/...` is (it resolves to `/private/var/...`), `module` is never inside any of those ancestors. The `source === "melian"` guard on line 143 then rejects the entry whatever line 140 does.
explanation.whatToDo: Write `const melian = await realpath(await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "melian-install-")));` (`realpath` from `node:fs/promises` is already mocked through to the actual one). Better still, also assert `expect(nodeUrl.fileURLToPath).toHaveReturnedWith(join(melian, "src", "mutation-enumeration.ts"))` so the test shows the scratch install was actually used.
explanation.whyHere: This change exists to move the fixture out of the checkout's `node_modules` without losing what the test checks. That is the line-140 rule that a fallback entry inside the reviewed root, but not in its `node_modules`, is refused. On a host with a symlinked tmpdir, the scratch tree makes the test pass for a different reason (the line-143 ancestor check), so it no longer guards line 140. The repository already knows this trap: `mutation-cache.test.ts:58`, `store-prune.test.ts:56`, `store-prune-rename.test.ts:25` and others wrap `mkdtemp(tmpdir())` in `realpath`. `mutation-enumeration.test.ts` is also not in `scripts/macos-tests.json`, so macOS CI would never notice.

properties.failureScenario: On macOS (`tmpdir()` = `/var/folders/xx/T`, realpath `/private/var/folders/xx/T`), delete line 140 of `packages/pipeline/src/mutation-enumeration.ts` (the `inside(root, module) && (!inside(install, module) || trackedInstall)` guard). In the "melian" iteration, `module` = `/private/var/folders/xx/T/melian-install-AB/node_modules/melian-review/repo/index.js`. The fake `fileURLToPath` returns `/var/folders/xx/T/melian-install-AB/src/mutation-enumeration.ts`, so `ancestorInstalls` yields `/var/folders/xx/T/melian-install-AB/node_modules`, `/var/folders/xx/T/node_modules`, …, `/node_modules`. `relative(...)` from each of them to `module` starts with `../`, so line 143 `continue`s. `open` then throws `MutationEnumerationError("instrumenter")` and the test still passes with the guard it names removed. On Linux, where `/tmp` is real, the same mutation makes `open` return an adapter and the test fails. The macOS outcome is inferred by reading `inside`/`ancestorInstalls`, not run.
